subject: physics
question_text: Write the relation between the escape velocity and the orbital velocity of a satellite revolving close to the earth.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two speeds
lines: For a satellite revolving close to the surface
steps.why: Both come from the same R, so the ratio between them is a pure number with no earth data in it.
common_mistakes: Using v₀ = √(2gR) and v_e = √(gR), the two the wrong way round.

recall.must_convey: That v naught is root g R and v e is root 2 g R.
reject: v e is root two times v naught

steps.memory_tip: Escape velocity has the 2 under the root: v_e = √(2gR). Orbital has none: v₀ = √(gR).
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both speeds out before you divide one by the other.

steps.label: The relation
lines: So escaping needs only about 1.4 times the
steps.why: The factor is surprisingly small, which is why a satellite already in orbit is most of the way to leaving the earth altogether.
common_mistakes: Saying the escape velocity is twice the orbital velocity.

recall.must_convey: That v e equals root two times v naught, about 1.4 times.

steps.memory_tip: √2 ≈ 1.41, and 7.9 × 1.41 ≈ 11.2 km s⁻¹. The two known speeds agree.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Box √2 × v₀ and say 1.4 times, not twice.

insider_note: Write v₀ = √(gR) and v_e = √(2gR) first — they carry the first mark, and v_e = √2 v₀ on its own answers only half.
